explanation:
Travel

In this Upper-intermediate Vocabulary Lesson about Travel, you will learn about different types of trips, journeys, and travel experiences. The pictures, descriptions, and examples below will help you understand and remember the terms.



1 Travel is usually a verb, but it can also be a noun. As a verb, to travel means to go from one place to another. As a noun, travel is uncountable and refers to the general activity of travelling.

  • How do you travel to work?
  • Air travel is expensive these days, so we tend to go everywhere by car.

2 A trip is always a noun, and it refers to the act of going on a visit to a place for a short time and returning.

  • We are planning a trip to London to visit my uncle in the spring.

3 A journey is the act of travelling from one place to another, so one trip implies two journeys.

  • We were all tired after our long journey.

4 A voyage is a journey that you take in a boat or on a ship.

  • The voyage across the ocean took just over two weeks.

5 Your destination is the place you intend to reach at the end of a journey or voyage.

  • It took us nearly two days to reach our destination.

6 The route is the path you take to get from your starting point to your destination.

  • We took a different route because the road we usually go on was closed.

7 A tour is a trip where you visit different places in a specific area.

  • Our tour of the pyramids was great; our guide was fantastic.

8 A road trip is a long journey that you make in a car or a bus.

  • Now that I have a car, I plan on taking a road trip to Scotland.

9 A business trip is a short trip that you make for work or business purposes.

  • My job involves a lot of business trips, many of which are overseas.

10 A pleasure trip is a trip that you take for personal enjoyment.

  • Unfortunately, this is not a pleasure trip, as I’ll be attending meetings every day.

11 A staycation is a holiday that you take in your own country instead of abroad.

  • My husband doesn’t enjoy flying, so our holidays are usually staycations in the countryside.

12 A city break is a short holiday in which you visit another city.

  • My girlfriend and I are planning a city break to Amsterdam next weekend.

13 Backpacking is the act of travelling with your possessions in a bag on your back.

  • After graduating from university, I spent a year backpacking through South America.

14 A pilgrimage is a journey that you make for religious purposes, usually to a sacred place.

  • More than 20,000 people make a pilgrimage to visit this shrine each year.

15 An eco-tour is a type of travel focused on protecting the natural environment.

  • We went on an eco-tour around a protected nature reserve.

16 A field trip is a school outing taken for educational purposes.

  • My history teacher is taking us on a field trip to see the ancient ruins.

17 A cruise is a voyage on a ship where you visit different places.

  • We stopped at various ports around the Mediterranean during our 10-day cruise.

18 A safari is an organised land journey in which you observe animals.

  • We saw some amazing wildlife on our safari last year.

19 A spa retreat is a short break focused on physical health, relaxation, and treatments.

  • I had lots of relaxing treatments during my spa retreat last month.

20 A flight is a journey you take through the air, usually by plane.

  • We arrived at the airport just in time to catch our flight.
Flashcards

After completing the exercises in this lesson on Travel, you can use the unit’s Vocabulary Flashcards to revise and help you memorize the terms.

We didn't have much money when I was growing up, so our holidays were usually 1 across the country in our very crowded car. In fact, the only time I went abroad was on a school 2 to Paris when I was fourteen. It was my first time in a plane, and I spent the whole 3 staring out the window, mesmerised by the clouds below.

At the age of 16, I started working and earning my own money. This enabled me to save up enough cash to travel to other countries. As soon as I left school, I went 4 with a friend around Europe for the summer. We did a lot of hiking, carrying everything we needed on our backs.

After I returned, I found a job working for an international clothing company, and one of the highlights of this job was that I got to take lots of 5 abroad to attend meetings and visit our factories. Although we never had much free time on these trips, I still enjoyed being somewhere different, and on a few occasions, I was able to extend my trip by an extra day or two and take a 6 around the place.

I got married when I was 30 to a woman who also loved travelling, and we spent our honeymoon on a 10-day 7 around the Mediterranean. My wife and I both had busy jobs, which left us little time to travel. However, on our first anniversary, I surprised her with a 8 to Rome which we both enjoyed.

Soon after that, we started a family, which meant that if we wanted to travel, we had to do things the kids would enjoy. When my son was four years old, we decided to take a family holiday to France, and instead of flying, we took a ferry across the English Channel. Unfortunately, my wife suffered from seasickness and spent the entire 9 in our cabin feeling too ill to enjoy the view. Luckily, things improved after that, and we spent a wonderful two weeks travelling around the country, stopping at various places of interest along the way.

Now that we have four children, travelling abroad is just too expensive, so our holidays consist of 10 , usually to the seaside. The kids really enjoy these breaks and spend every day at the beach, no matter what the weather is like. I don't know when I'll next have the opportunity to travel abroad and see more of the world, though I'm sure I will one day. For now, however, I am happy to stay at home and enjoy the unpredictable English weather.
